acceptedInterpretation: The story faithfully elaborates the original intent by tracing the single reported symptom (malformed versionless record crashes enforce gate) to its root cause (no validation between JSON.parse and the typed domain) and covering the full blast radius: malformed records, malformed envelopes, non-object JSON roots silently misread as absent, unparseable files, and all ten production consumers. Each extension was discovered during the pre-story cross-host adversarial audit and explicitly approved by the operator in the same session that produced the original request. The hard constraint (MUST NOT change any valid v1 verdict) was refined — not weakened — to scope validity to records well-formed under the legacy v1 schema, because the original wording is self-contradictory under the operator-approved full validation (section 8.1 of the decision document). The migration scan (D-7) mechanically proves the affected set is empty rather than assuming it. The two-layer fix (read-boundary validation primary, predicate guard as defense-in-depth) is a documented departure from the original pick-ONE suggestion, justified by the recoverability analysis in section 9. The acceptance claim bundles four corruption classes plus the invariance digest, but all stem from one root cause and one mechanism, and the RED artifact pins every class so partial delivery cannot be claimed as success.
notes: ASSESSMENT DETAIL — (1) normalizedOutcome vs sourceText: The sourceText itself records operator approval of full validation, quarantine, and migration scan. The growth from one malformed-record symptom to four corruption classes plus ten consumers is root-cause tracing, not scope drift. Every addition was discovered during the pre-story audit (cross-host adversarial, six findings upheld) or the PLAN scope review (three gap items added: CHK-009 order independence, CHK-010 must-not-change assertions, CHK-011 fuzz property). The fuzz property in particular addresses the meta-level lesson: enumerated test rows prove known cases but not unknown ones, which is the same blind spot that produced the original defect. (2) acceptanceClaim bundling: Technically a bundle of four corruption classes plus invariance digest, but acceptable because all share one root cause and one fix mechanism (read-boundary validation with quarantine). The RED artifact (CHK-001) pins specific assertion shapes for each class (CRASH: bare TypeError; SILENT: wrong observable value with no throw; UNTYPED-THROW: raw SyntaxError). Partial delivery would leave RED rows still failing. (3) Hard constraint: Section 8.1 demonstrates the original wording is self-contradictory under full validation — it forbids any previously-SATISFIED record from changing while full validation would necessarily flip schema-invalid-but-currently-satisfying records. The refinement to well-formed records is the only logically consistent reading. The migration scan (D-7, REQUIRED before merge) is the mechanical proof, not an assumption. The PLAN-phase scan found 0 affected records across 105 artifacts and 144 records, but the scan is committed and re-runnable at merge time (CHK-003 adversarial intent explicitly forbids hard-coding the PLAN-phase snapshot). On principle the reinterpretation is legitimate: a schema-invalid record satisfying the gate is a latent bug, not a valid verdict. (4) Competing interpretations: The decision document section 6.2 analyzed all three candidate layers and explained why A alone (predicate guard) leaves corruption invisible and why B/C alone (read-boundary) breaks recoverability. Decision D-2 explicitly documents the two-layer choice. The scope-boundary confirms CHK-005 is defense-in-depth only. No interpretation was silently dropped. Considered and rejected passing with caveats: the acceptanceClaim could be more explicit about requiring ALL four classes, but the enumeration in the claim text serves that purpose.
